subject: Science
title: Show what we know again
objectives: Children will show Term 2 learning through play stations.
Teachers will gather evidence for every child’s Term 2 record.
content: Revising animals and homes, plants and seeds, and caring and food through play stations and gathering Term 2 evidence.
teachingActivities: Keep every activity familiar and playful; observe quietly and record without interrupting; offer help only when a child is stuck; celebrate what each child can do.
learnerActivities: Show what they know about animals, plants, seeds, food and caring through play.
assessment: Observe and record each child’s Term 2 science learning using the four-level scale.
expectedOutcomes: Completes familiar tasks with growing independence.
Each child has an observation record for Term 2.

lessons.title: Revising animals and homes
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will revisit animals, their homes and their babies through games.
successCriteria: Matches animals to homes and babies
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt about animals, their homes and babies, plants and seeds, food and caring this term.
lessons.starter: Sing the animal song and say "Today we play our favourite animal games."
teacherActivities: Play find your mother with baby cards.
Move like animals to the drum.
Let each child choose a favourite game.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Play the home matching game. Children: Children match animals to homes.
Step 2. Teacher: Play find your mother with baby cards. Children: Children match babies to mothers.
Step 3. Teacher: Move like animals to the drum. Children: Children move like animals.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child choose a favourite game. Children: Child chooses and plays.

practical.title: Animal games
steps: Children play each for four minutes.
The teacher notes who names animals and homes.
practical.safety: Keep the floor clear and supervise movement. Use soft toys and large cards.

differentiation.support: Play with the child and use three animals.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to lead a game.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What is the baby of a cow?

expectedOutcomes: Matches animals to homes and babies
teacherReflection: Which children could show "revisit animals, their homes and their babies through games" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Revising plants and seeds
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will revisit plants, seeds, leaves, flowers and fruits.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt about animals, their homes and babies, plants and seeds, food and caring this term.
lessons.starter: Look at the seeds we planted and say "Let us see what has grown."
teacherActivities: Look at the growing seeds and talk about changes.
Sort leaves into big and small.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Look at the growing seeds and talk about changes. Children: Children look and say grow.
Step 2. Teacher: Sort leaves into big and small. Children: Child sorts the leaves.
Step 3. Teacher: Match fruits to trees. Children: Child matches fruit to tree.
Step 4. Teacher: Water the plants together. Children: Child waters a plant.

practical.title: Plants and seeds
steps: The teacher notes names and care.
practical.safety: Wash hands after touching plants and soil. Keep floors dry.

differentiation.support: Look together and name each plant.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to explain how a seed grows.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Wash hands and say thank you.
lessons.homeConnection: Keep watching plants grow at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "revisit plants, seeds, leaves, flowers and fruits" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Revising caring and food
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will revisit caring for living things and foods from plants and animals.
successCriteria: Sorts foods into plant and animal
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt about animals, their homes and babies, plants and seeds, food and caring this term.
lessons.starter: Say "Today we care for living things and talk about food."
teacherActivities: Sort food pictures into plant and animal foods.
Water a plant and care for a toy pet.
Choose foods for a healthy plate.
Say how we are kind to animals.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Sort food pictures into plant and animal foods. Children: Child sorts the foods.
Step 2. Teacher: Water a plant and care for a toy pet. Children: Child waters and cares gently.
Step 3. Teacher: Choose foods for a healthy plate. Children: Child chooses healthy foods.
Step 4. Teacher: Say how we are kind to animals. Children: Child says kind or gentle.

practical.title: Care and food
steps: The teacher notes sorting and gentle care.
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep floors dry. Use soft toys and pictures.

differentiation.support: Offer two choices at each station.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to tell a friend how to look after a plant.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Sorts foods by where they come from
lessons.homeConnection: Care for plants and pets at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "revisit caring for living things and foods from plants and animals" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Living things play stations
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Teachers will gather evidence of each child’s Term 2 science learning at play stations.
successCriteria: Completes familiar tasks with growing independence
Shows animal, plant, food and caring knowledge
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt about animals, their homes and babies, plants and seeds, food and caring this term.
lessons.starter: Sing a favourite song and show six stations to the class.
teacherActivities: Set up six stations: animals, homes, babies, seeds, food and caring.
Observe each child at two stations and record what they can do.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up six stations: animals, homes, babies, seeds, food and caring. Children: Children rotate every three minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: Observe each child at two stations and record what they can do. Children: Children play at stations.
Step 3. Teacher: Take photographs and make notes. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Six stations
steps: Set up six stations with familiar materials.
practical.safety: Supervise each station with an adult or helper. Keep floors dry and clear.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and stay at familiar stations.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to show friends how a station works.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: names animals; matches animals to homes; names plants; waters a plant; sorts foods; handles animals gently.

lessons.conclusion: Say well done and wave goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Play a favourite game from this term at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will gather evidence of each child’s Term 2 science learning at play stations" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Term 2 science celebration
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will celebrate Term 2 with songs, plants and games, and teachers will complete their records.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt about animals, their homes and babies, plants and seeds, food and caring this term.
lessons.starter: Say "Today we celebrate. Let us look at our plants and sing our favourite songs."
teacherActivities: Look at the plants we grew and talk about how they changed.
Give each child a sticker or praise and say their name.
learnerActivities: Children join in and choose a song.
Child waves and says thank you.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Sing favourite songs with actions. Children: Children join in and choose a song.
Step 2. Teacher: Look at the plants we grew and talk about how they changed. Children: Children look and say grow.
Step 3. Teacher: Give each child a sticker or praise and say their name. Children: Child waves and says thank you.

practical.title: Celebration circle
steps: Sing and look at the plants.
practical.safety: Check for allergies before any snack and use non-toxic stickers. Supervise closely.

differentiation.support: Hold the child’s hand and sing along.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to choose the last song.

assessment.method: Complete each child’s Term 2 science record using today’s observations and the week’s notes. Record a next step for Term 3.

questions.question: What is your favourite plant or animal?
Did you like our plants?
questions.expected: Yes with a smile or word.

lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say "See you in Term 3."
lessons.homeConnection: Keep exploring plants and animals during the holiday.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "celebrate Term 2 with songs, plants and games, and teachers will complete their records" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
